listen.explanationKey: What amendment says all persons born or naturalized in the United States, and subject to the jurisdiction thereof, are U.S. citizens?
facts: After the Civil War, the 14th Amendment said that all persons born or naturalized in the United States are citizens.
In 1870, the 15th Amendment said a man could not be kept from voting because of his race.
But for almost one hundred years after that, many Black Americans were still kept from voting by unfair rules and violence. The civil rights movement fought to change this.

a group of people, often by skin color or where their families come from

readIt.sentence: Who has the right to vote?

writeIt.sentence: Citizens have the right to vote.

listen.explanationKey: Name one leader of the women’s rights movement in the 1800s.
facts: In the 1800s, women could not vote in most of the country.
Susan B. Anthony and Elizabeth Cady Stanton led the fight for women's right to vote.

Sojourner Truth and Harriet Tubman were born into slavery and escaped. They spoke out for the rights of women and of Black Americans. Harriet Tubman also helped many enslaved people escape to freedom.
In 1920, after World War I, the 19th Amendment gave women the right to vote.

newWords.meaning: a group of people working together for a change
the amendment that gave women the right to vote
